title: Can we find these eight differences?
description: Eight differences of decimals are found one by one. The points are lined up, a whole number is written with zeroes, and one unit of the next place is broken wherever a digit is too small. Each answer is checked by adding the smaller number back.
teaching_notes: One idea: write both numbers with the same places, then subtract from the right, breaking from the next place when a digit is too small. Watch for students who ignore the missing zeroes.

source: Figure it Out (adding and subtracting decimals), Q2
video_script.why: The child has subtracted with a break in one place and in two places, and now does a full set with whole numbers and short decimals in the mix.
video_script.substitution: Write both numbers with the same places, subtract from the right, and break one unit of the next place when a digit is too small.
video_script.anchor: Eight differences of decimal numbers, listed on the board.
video_script.payoff_line: Write the whole number with the same places as the other number

final_answer.spoken: three point three, nine point two, five point nine, zero point eight zero two, sixteen point nine five, sixteen point four zero five, zero point eight one and five point seven four nine

video_script.design: The eight pairs stay in a column on the board. Each pair is rewritten with matching places, the broken units are shown moving right as ten, and the check adds the smaller number back to land on the larger.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about eight differences.
<bookmark mark='ab'/>Five point six minus two point three. Eighteen minus eight point eight.
<bookmark mark='cd'/>Ten point four minus four point five. Seventeen minus sixteen point one nine eight.
<bookmark mark='ef'/>Seventeen minus zero point zero five. Thirty four point five zero five minus eighteen point one.
<bookmark mark='gh'/>Nine point nine minus nine point zero nine. Six point two three six minus zero point four eight seven.

marks.given: the eight pairs are written in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eight pairs of decimal numbers, as shown on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the difference for each pair.

marks.b: (b) 18 becomes 18.0 and one unit breaks into ten tenths

beats.colours: the broken unit in a new colour
beats.moves_through: one unit moves right as ten tenths
narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, the first three. Six take away three is three, and five take away two is three. That is three point three.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Write eighteen as eighteen point zero, and break one unit into ten tenths.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>Ten take away eight is two, and seventeen take away eight is nine. That is nine point two.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Ten point four is nine units and fourteen tenths. Fourteen take away five is nine, and nine take away four is five. That is five point nine.

marks.d: (d) 17 becomes 17.000 and breaks into 6 units, 9 tenths, 9 hundredths and 10 thousandths
marks.e: (e) 17 becomes 17.00 and breaks into 16 units, 9 tenths and 10 hundredths

beats.colours: the broken units in a new colour
beats.moves_through: one unit moves right through the zeroes as ten, then nine, then nine
narration: <bookmark mark='d'/>Step two. Write seventeen as seventeen point zero zero zero. Break from the units, and the places after it hold nine, nine and ten.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Ten take away eight is two.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>Nine take away nine is none, and nine take away one is eight. Six take away six is none, so zero point eight zero two.
<bookmark mark='e'/>Write seventeen as seventeen point zero zero. The same break leaves sixteen, nine and ten.
<bookmark mark='e2'/>Ten take away five is five, so sixteen point nine five.

marks.f: (f) 18.1 becomes 18.100 and the first three places are subtracted
marks.f2: one ten breaks into ten units
marks.g2: one tenth breaks into ten hundredths; 10 - 9 = 1 and 8 - 0 = 8, giving 0.81
marks.h: (h) three breaks happen one after another

beats.colours: the broken units in a new colour
beats.moves_through: one unit moves right as ten
narration: <bookmark mark='f'/>Step three. Write eighteen point one as eighteen point one zero zero. The first three places need no break.
<bookmark mark='f2'/>Four units is too few, so break one ten.
<bookmark mark='f3'/>Fourteen take away eight is six, and two tens take away one ten is one ten. That is sixteen point four zero five.
<bookmark mark='g'/>Write nine point nine as nine point nine zero.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Break one tenth into ten hundredths. Ten take away nine is one, and eight take away nothing is eight. That is zero point eight one.
<bookmark mark='h'/>In the last pair, three places break one after another.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>Sixteen take away seven is nine, and twelve take away eight is four.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>Eleven take away four is seven, and five take away nothing is five. That is five point seven four nine.

beats.on_screen: check: 3.3 + 2.3 = 5.6; 9.2 + 8.8 = 18.0; the other six also add back to the first number

marks.check: each answer is added to the smaller number
marks.rest: the other six sums are written and each lands on the first number

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check each answer by adding the smaller number back.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Three point three plus two point three is five point six. Nine point two plus eight point eight is eighteen.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other six sums also land on the first number of their pair.

narration: <bookmark mark='payoff'/>Write the whole number with the same places as the other number.
<bookmark mark='ans1'/>The first three are three point three, nine point two and five point nine.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Then zero point eight zero two and sixteen point nine five.
<bookmark mark='ans3'/>Then sixteen point four zero five, zero point eight one and five point seven four nine.
